messages.subject: Questions?
parts:
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am a beginner in using distance program for analyses of my study (line transect based study on primates). I had already downloaded it, also followed the "Online distance sampling course" which is fluently & interestingly presented and very helpful for users, I have honesty to appreciate all of you guys! Here with my comments, i have few questions in which i'm not clear to the notion of "A = size of region of interest", in regarded to, "a = area of “covered” region = 2wL, what i shortly would like to ask you is that my study area is a national park (having a total area of 514 square kilometer, but my study only covers 21.2 square kilometer of the park area (only one stratum of the park), which is the frosted part, and where monkeys are/were habituated than the other area of the park (I used 17 line transects in this stratum).
So, in my case:
1) Is "A" equal to the whole study area of the park (514 km2) (or= to sampled area; one stratum of the park=21.2 km 2)? 2) which of the two areas i will have to consider it as A through my data analysis?
3) If the answer i would consider as a is 21.2 km2 , so can i also estimate the monkeys abundance and/or density using 514 km2 (i.e., over the entire park area)? I am just on analysis stage of my data using distance program. I really appreciate your faster response/answer asap! thank you so much!

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Questions?
parts:
Solomon (list)

I've placed my answer to Solomon's question in the Disqus forum where he asked the question.  He asked his question a second time to this list, but I've answered it in its original location (https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/contact/)

I intend to answer questions raised from the online course at the online course web pages.

---

Solomon

Really happy to hear you are getting good use out of the online materials.  That's why we posted them.

You ask a good question about the meaning of "A" defined as the size of the region of interest.  This can often be a source of confusion for researchers.  The short answer to your question is A=21.2km^2. 

This is because you only sampled one stratum of the park, all of your transects were located in that stratum.  Consequently, you cannot make inference to the remaining strata in the park because your study design made it impossible for sampling effort (transects) to fall into the remaining strata.  Your study will allow you to make inference about only the stratum where you sampled.  Consequently, the "size of the region of interest" in your study is the size if that single stratum, not the size of the entire park.


Let us know if you have more questions.
